newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russian inflation dips to seven-month low.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russian inflation dips to seven-month low.

text.p: Russia's monthly inflation rate slowed in April to its lowest level in seven months, according to official figures released on Wednesday.
The State Statistics Committee said consumer prices rose by 1.0 percent in April after 1.4 percent in March.
That is the lowest rise since a 0.3 percent increase in September last year, shortly after low seasonal food prices resulted in consumer prices actually falling in the summer.
The committee said prices have risen by 6.4 percent so far this year, more than half the entire 1997 increase forecast by the government.
But Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said in Washington on Tuesday that inflation was completely under control and the 12 percent target would be met. Inflation was 22 percent in 1996.
Inflation has been slowing since January, when a number of price rises in public services, traditionally implemented at the start of the year, caused a spike in the trend.
Annual inflation was still in triple digits 15 months ago, but a tight monetary policy and stable rouble have brought it down sharply.

The government's inability to pay many public-sector wages and pensions, because tax revenues are much lower than budgeted, also means many people do not have money to buy as much as they want, dampening demand for goods which could push up prices.
Chubais's confidence that inflation will continue to slow was reflected in the central bank's decision to cut its refinancing rate on Monday to 36 percent from 42 percent.

Interest rates in the market place are coming down too. The yield on a 322-day Treasury bill auctioned on Wednesday averaged 30.64 percent, down from 31.77 percent at an auction of 364-day paper a week ago.
